title: At a Winter Window
description: Look through a winter window using familiar words for its parts, nearby surfaces, and outdoor details.
cardDescription: Look through a winter window using familiar words for its parts, nearby surfaces, and outdoor details.
focus: The clues distinguish the built frame from what appears on or beyond the glass. Location identifies several small parts.
solvingTip: Check whether a clue asks for a window part, a light effect, or a cold-weather form.
words: One sheet of glass fitted into a window
Structure supporting the edges of a window
Transparent material through which the outdoor view is seen
Horizontal ledge at the bottom of a window
Fabric panel hung beside a window
Small fastening holding a window closed
Ice crystals forming a pattern on a cold surface
Solid with an orderly structure, as one piece of frost
Hanging taper of ice formed from dripping water
Upper covering seen above a house’s walls
Lower roof edge projecting beyond a wall
Darker area formed where light is blocked

answerNotes.PANE: Pane is the glass-sheet spelling. It sounds like pain but has a different meaning.
answerNotes.SILL: A sill is the bottom ledge. It differs from the surrounding upright frame.
answerNotes.EAVE: An eave is a projecting roof edge. The word is commonly encountered in the plural, eaves.
answerNotes.LATCH: The latch secures a movable window. It is different from the glass and the supporting frame.

title: A Snowman in the Yard
description: Picture a familiar winter display through simple shapes, clothing, and traditional snowman details.
cardDescription: Picture a familiar winter display through simple shapes, clothing, and traditional snowman details.
focus: The clues identify objects and body-like shapes in a seasonal scene. Direct descriptions keep the focus on everyday words.
solvingTip: Look for a shape, a clothing item, or something used to represent a feature.
words: Human-shaped figure formed from packed snow
Frozen flakes packed together for a winter figure
Rounded shape used as a snowman’s body section
Main lower structure supporting a snowman’s head
Upper round part holding a snowman’s face
Tapered vegetable traditionally used for a snowman’s nose
Small disk used to suggest a snowman’s front fastening
Long cloth placed around a snow figure’s neck
Head covering placed on top of a snowman
Thin piece of wood used to suggest an arm
Black fuel traditionally used for a snowman’s eyes
Arrangement of features on the figure’s head
Upturned mouth shape in a cheerful display
Curved on all sides like a snowball

answerNotes.CARROT: The carrot supplies a familiar pointed nose shape. The clue uses a traditional display rather than an ingredient in a meal.
answerNotes.COAL: Coal is the dark material in this clue. It names an object used to represent eyes in a traditional image.
answerNotes.BUTTON: Button names a small disk here. It is separate from the whole item of clothing it might ordinarily fasten.
answerNotes.ROUND: Round is a shape description in this clue. It does not mean a stage of play or a musical form.

title: Music at the Skating Rink
description: Visit an indoor rink through familiar skating equipment, movements, and objects beside the ice.
cardDescription: Visit an indoor rink through familiar skating equipment, movements, and objects beside the ice.
focus: The clues identify equipment and simple movement words. They do not prescribe a skating routine.
solvingTip: Look for a whole item, one part, or an action on the ice.
words: Boot fitted with a blade for moving over ice
Narrow metal part beneath an ice skate
Cord used to fasten a skating boot
Foot-covering portion of an ice skate
Hand covering worn during a cold outing
Neck covering worn beside a winter rink
To move smoothly over the ice
Narrow working side of a skate blade
Place where a visitor can sit beside a rink
Long seat used when putting on skates
Organized sound played during a public skating session

answerNotes.BLADE: The blade is the metal part beneath the boot. Skate names the complete piece of footwear.
answerNotes.LACE: Lace means a fastening cord here. It does not name delicate openwork fabric.
answerNotes.RINK: A rink is the skating area. It differs from the individual blade or boot used on it.
answerNotes.GLIDE: Glide describes smooth movement. The clue asks for an action rather than an item of equipment.

title: Warm Things in the Cupboard
description: Open a winter cupboard through familiar fabrics, blankets, and smaller clothing items.
cardDescription: Open a winter cupboard through familiar fabrics, blankets, and smaller clothing items.
focus: The clues distinguish materials from the objects made with them. Some common words have a special household meaning.
solvingTip: Check whether the clue asks for a fabric, a covering, or something worn.
words: Large soft covering used for warmth
Layered fabric covering held together with stitching
Soft napped fabric used in many casual warm garments
Soft woven fabric with a brushed surface
Fiber obtained from a sheep’s coat
Plant fiber used in many woven household fabrics
Small blanket kept over a chair or sofa
Broad wrap worn over the shoulders
Long narrow covering worn around the neck
Hand covering with one shared finger section
Hand covering with separate finger sections

answerNotes.THROW: Throw is a small blanket here. It is not the act of tossing an object.
answerNotes.FLANNEL: Flannel is a fabric with a soft brushed surface. The word identifies a material rather than a specific garment.
answerNotes.SHAWL: A shawl covers the shoulders. Its width and position distinguish it from a narrow scarf.
answerNotes.MITTEN: A mitten places the fingers together. A glove gives each finger its own section.

title: A Pot of Winter Soup
description: Gather familiar soup ingredients, liquid bases, and serving objects for a winter meal.
cardDescription: Gather familiar soup ingredients, liquid bases, and serving objects for a winter meal.
focus: The clues identify foods and utensils. Direct definitions distinguish the liquid base from the finished dish.
solvingTip: Look for an ingredient, a vessel, or a serving implement.
words: Liquid-based dish served in a bowl
Savory liquid made by simmering ingredients in water
Flavorful cooking liquid used as a base for soup
Thick dish of ingredients cooked together in liquid
Edible seed added to many hearty soups
Small flat pulse used in a familiar soup
Grain often served as chewy pearls in soup
Deep cooking vessel holding a soup
Deep-bowled utensil used to serve a liquid dish
Rounded dish holding an individual soup serving
Eating utensil used for a liquid meal
Tapered root vegetable cut into many soups
Layered bulb vegetable used as a savory ingredient
Crisp-stalked vegetable used in many soup mixtures

answerNotes.STOCK: Stock is a cooking liquid in this clue. It does not mean merchandise or company shares.
answerNotes.LENTIL: A lentil is a small pulse. It identifies an ingredient rather than a grain such as barley.
answerNotes.LADLE: A ladle has a deep bowl for serving liquid. It is larger than the spoon used by one diner.
answerNotes.STEW: A stew is generally thicker than a soup. The words can overlap in everyday use, so the clue gives the intended texture.
